draft.title: Reactants and products
card: In a chemical reaction, new substances form. The substances you start with are the reactants.
The new substances that form are the products. They have different properties from the reactants.
A word equation names them with an arrow between: reactants → products. The arrow means "react to form".
Reactants are on the left of the arrow and products are on the right. If more than one substance is on a side, a plus sign joins them.
draft.remember: Reactants go in on the left of the arrow. Products come out on the right.

a.q: Which part of this word equation is a product? magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide
a.why: Magnesium oxide is on the right of the arrow, so it is the new substance that forms. Magnesium and oxygen are on the left, so they are the reactants that are used up.
a.clue: Look at which side of the arrow it is on.

b.q: Sam burns methane gas in a camp stove. The word equation is methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Which pair are both reactants?
b.why: Reactants are the substances on the left of the arrow, which are the ones that start the reaction. Carbon dioxide and water are on the right, so they are the products that form.
b.clue: Reactants are written before the arrow.
